Before you start

Say this to Claude once:

After each step from now on, commit, and add a row to PROCESS.md: the step, what the tool did, and what I decided.

The content: gstack

Open gstack’s /office-hours and say:

Help me write the content of my program’s promo page.

gstack makes the content of your page. Then Impeccable gives it its look.

Install Impeccable

Open Claude Code and say:

Install Impeccable from impeccable.style.

impeccable.style, Install.

Impeccable, step by step

Step What it does
1 shape a design brief for your page; no code yet
2 generate variants of your page in your browser; you pick one
3 critique looks at your page as a classmate, your teacher, and a stranger; names its weakest part

shape and generate, on the Cassino

The words did not change. What changed: which three words you remember.

What will trip you up

  • Impeccable’s detector refuses overused fonts (Fraunces, Inter, Roboto …). Let it.
  • generate happens in your browser: keep the page open, and pick there.

Before you publish

GitHub Pages publishes everything in the folder, to anyone, and the repository must be public.

  • No personal data: bank statements, photos of faces, real names.
  • Deleting a file is not enough: it stays in the git history.
  • If something got in, ask me. Rewriting history is possible, but it is a separate job.

GitHub Docs: “Removing sensitive data from a repository”.

Your video

30 seconds: your sentence, moving

  • Three beats, one for each part of your sentence.
  • Real screens from your program.
  • No sound needed. One line of text at a time.
  • It lives on your page, not in your presentation.

Making it

Open Claude Code and say:

Install HyperFrames from github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes. Then make a 30-second promo video from my promo page.

It needs Node 22+ and FFmpeg. If it won’t start: record your screen, and add captions.

github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes, README. Cassino video: hyperframes 0.9.26.

Your demo day

1 and 8 December

Five minutes each. A presentation, not a live run.

Everyone else in the room is your audience.

Come to both days.

“The second half of the semester”, Canvas announcement, 18 October 2026.

Five minutes, five slides

Slide
1 Who it is for, and why
2 Your demo: what goes in, what comes out — screenshots from a real run
3 Why it works: one check you did yourself — a test, a known answer, or a refusal
4 What you learned
5 What’s next: where you would take it from here

One minute per slide. No title slide: your name goes on the first one.

Slide 4: what you learned

Choose one

  • A. One moment the agent got it wrong, and how you noticed.
  • B. One decision the agent could not make for you.
  • C. What you would do differently in your next project.

Make it concrete

  • One moment, from your own repository.
  • A commit, a test, a log entry, a change request: something I can open.

The rules for your slides

  • Every screenshot from a real run of your program. An illustration is labelled as one.
  • Every number has a source: a run, a file, a test.
  • No speaker notes in the published deck: on GitHub Pages anyone can read them in the page source.
  • It opens from one address. We project from one shared computer, and I link every deck from esst-prog2.github.io.

Where your slides go

One address for everyone:

esst-prog2.github.io/your-repo/slides/

Your page is published Put your slides in
from the /docs folder docs/slides/index.html
from the root of main slides/index.html
by a GitHub Actions build (Vite, …) the folder it copies as it is, e.g. public/slides/index.html
